title: Low sets and a low simple set

based_on.title: Lecture notes in Computability Theory
based_on.pages: December 3, 2008 version; section 29, Theorem 29.1, pp. 58–60; fixed-certificate stage implementation expanded

summary: Control an enumerable set's own oracle-halting problem while meeting every simplicity requirement, producing a noncomputable set whose jump has only the ordinary halting degree.
abstract: An oracle can answer membership questions that no ordinary program can decide, yet add no strength to the first halting problem. Such an oracle is called low: halting for programs that use it is equivalent to ordinary halting. We construct a low enumerable set whose complement is infinite but contains no infinite enumerable subset. The construction adds a witness whenever an infinite enumerable set needs to be met, while protecting selected successful oracle computations from later changes. Higher-priority additions can destroy protection, but each fixed requirement suffers only finitely many such injuries. The surviving records give computable guesses that converge to the set's jump. The resulting set is simple, noncomputable, and strictly weaker than the ordinary halting set.
